title: The gerund: two things at once

sections.content: You know the *gerund* for parallel and simultaneous actions from B1 Unit 2. The gerund says how or while the main verb happens, and the person is the same. It fits the campaigns of Bolívar and San Martín, which advanced while doing something else. The gerund does not change: *subiendo*, *venciendo*.

items.spanish: Los soldados cruzaron los Andes subiendo por caminos de montaña.
items.english: The soldiers crossed the Andes going up mountain paths.

items.spanish: Bolívar avanzó por el norte venciendo a los realistas.
items.english: Bolívar advanced through the north defeating the royalists.

items.spanish: San Martín preparó el ejército en Mendoza formando soldados.
items.english: San Martín prepared the army in Mendoza training soldiers.

items.spanish: Los dos generales avanzaron desde direcciones opuestas, buscando el mismo objetivo.
items.english: The two generals advanced from opposite directions, looking for the same aim.

sections.content: The gerund has the same subject as the main verb: *Bolívar avanzó venciendo* means Bolívar did both. The tense comes from the main verb only.
